## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Solids CSG
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Union, intersection, and difference of polygon soups
//  - Polygon-versus-plane classification and splitting
//  - Point-in-solid parity and fragmenting against a solid
//  - Deformation body for the polygon-soup solid

library SolidsCsg
{
    //==
    // # Union, intersection, and difference of polygon soups
    //
    // Boolean operations on closed `PolygonSoup3D` solids, the plane-clip
    // re-expression of csg.js: every boolean output is assembled from fragments of
    // A's faces cut by B's planes (so no fragment straddles B's boundary — see the
    // clipping section) and kept by whether the fragment's
    // centroid lies inside or outside B, plus the symmetric fragments of B against
    // A. Correct-over-fast: a boolean costs O(|A|^2 |B| + |B|^2 |A|); a BSP-tree
    // variant is a later, separate pass.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_solid_geometry)
    //
    // Precondition throughout: both solids are closed, with convex CCW-outward
    // faces. Exactly coplanar shared faces of the two solids are the known
    // unreliable case (their fragment centroids sit ON the other boundary).

    // The fragments of a's faces, cut by b's planes, whose centroid's
    // insideness of b equals `keepInside`. The centroid of a convex fragment is
    // interior to it, so it classifies the whole fragment.
    KeptFragments(a: PolygonSoup3D, b: PolygonSoup3D, keepInside: Boolean): Array<Polygon3D>
        => a.Fragments(b.Planes, Number.CsgPlaneTolerance)
            .FlatMap(f => KeepPolygon(b.Contains(f.Centroid).ExclusiveOr(keepInside).Not, f));

    // The polygon turned inside out: reversed winding flips its outward normal.
    ReversedWinding(p: Polygon3D): Polygon3D
        => Polygon3D(p.Points.Count.MapRange(i => p.Points[p.Points.Count - 1 - i]));

    // A | B: the surface of A outside B, plus the surface of B outside A.
    Union(a: PolygonSoup3D, b: PolygonSoup3D): PolygonSoup3D
        => PolygonSoup3D(a.KeptFragments(b, false).Concatenate(b.KeptFragments(a, false)));

    // A & B: the surface of A inside B, plus the surface of B inside A.
    Intersection(a: PolygonSoup3D, b: PolygonSoup3D): PolygonSoup3D
        => PolygonSoup3D(a.KeptFragments(b, true).Concatenate(b.KeptFragments(a, true)));

    // A - B: the surface of A outside B, plus the surface of B inside A turned
    // inside out, so it faces into the carved cavity.
    Difference(a: PolygonSoup3D, b: PolygonSoup3D): PolygonSoup3D
        => PolygonSoup3D(a.KeptFragments(b, false)
            .Concatenate(b.KeptFragments(a, true).Map(f => f.ReversedWinding)));

    //==
    // # Polygon-versus-plane classification and splitting
    //
    // The foundational CSG primitives on the types in `solids.types.plato`:
    // the supporting plane of a convex polygon, the four-way polygon/plane
    // classification, and Sutherland-Hodgman clipping of a convex polygon to a
    // half-space and splitting by a plane.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutherland%E2%80%93Hodgman_algorithm)
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * Every polygon is CONVEX and planar with CCW-outward winding
    //     (`PolygonSoup3D`'s invariant); clipping a non-convex ring is not defined
    //     here.
    //   * The plane's FRONT is its positive half-space (`lines.types.plato`);
    //     clipping keeps the front, boundary inclusive.

    // The on-plane thickness for polygon/plane classification: a vertex within
    // this absolute distance of a plane counts as lying ON it. One shared knob
    // rather than a magic number in each body.
    CsgPlaneTolerance(_: Number): Number
        => 0.00000001;

    // The plane a planar polygon lies in, facing the polygon's outward normal.
    SupportingPlane(p: Polygon3D): Plane
        => FromPointNormal(p.Points.First, p.Normal);

    // How the polygon sits relative to the plane, with vertices within
    // `tolerance` of the plane counting as on it: Spanning when vertices lie
    // strictly on both sides, otherwise the side any strict vertex lies on,
    // otherwise Coplanar.
    RelationTo(p: Polygon3D, pl: Plane, tolerance: Number): PlaneRelation3D
    {
        var anyFront = p.Points.Any(q => pl.SignedDistance(q) > tolerance);
        var anyBack = p.Points.Any(q => pl.SignedDistance(q) < -tolerance);
        return anyFront && anyBack
            ? PlaneRelation3D.Spanning
            : (anyFront
                ? PlaneRelation3D.Front
                : (anyBack ? PlaneRelation3D.Back : PlaneRelation3D.Coplanar));
    }

    // A 0- or 1-element list: the point when `condition` holds, else empty.
    // The keep-or-drop building block inside a FlatMap (A1: no Optional<T>).
    KeepPoint(condition: Boolean, p: Point3D): Array<Point3D>
        => (condition ? 1 : 0).MapRange(i => p);

    // A 0- or 1-element list: the polygon when `condition` holds, else empty.
    KeepPolygon(condition: Boolean, p: Polygon3D): Array<Polygon3D>
        => (condition ? 1 : 0).MapRange(i => p);

    // Where the segment (a, b) meets the plane. Meaningful only when the
    // endpoints lie strictly on opposite sides (the interpolant is then in
    // (0, 1)); a same-side or coplanar segment yields an unusable point the
    // caller must drop.
    CrossingPoint(pl: Plane, a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Point3D
        => a.Lerp(b, pl.SignedDistance(a) / (pl.SignedDistance(a) - pl.SignedDistance(b)));

    // The vertices edge (a -> b) contributes to the ring clipped to the plane's
    // front half-space: a itself when a is on or in front of the plane, then
    // the crossing point when the edge changes sides.
    ClipEdge(pl: Plane, a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Array<Point3D>
        => KeepPoint(pl.SignedDistance(a) >= 0.0, a)
            .Concatenate(KeepPoint(
                (pl.SignedDistance(a) >= 0.0).ExclusiveOr(pl.SignedDistance(b) >= 0.0),
                pl.CrossingPoint(a, b)));

    // The convex polygon restricted to the plane's front half-space
    // (Sutherland-Hodgman against a single plane): each edge contributes its
    // kept endpoint and its crossing point, in ring order. May yield a ring of
    // fewer than three vertices when the polygon lies behind the plane.
    ClipToHalfSpace(p: Polygon3D, pl: Plane): Polygon3D
        => Polygon3D(p.Points.Count.MapRange(i => i)
            .FlatMap(i => pl.ClipEdge(p.Points[i], p.Points.AtModulo(i + 1))));

    // The polygon as a 0- or 1-element list: dropped when its ring has fewer
    // than three vertices and so bounds no area.
    NonDegenerate(p: Polygon3D): Array<Polygon3D>
        => KeepPolygon(p.Points.Count >= 3, p);

    // The polygon split by the plane into its non-degenerate pieces: itself,
    // uncut, when it does not span the plane (a coplanar polygon is kept once,
    // not clipped into both half-spaces), otherwise its front piece followed by
    // its back piece.
    SplitByPlane(p: Polygon3D, pl: Plane, tolerance: Number): Array<Polygon3D> =>
        match (p.RelationTo(pl, tolerance)) {
            Front => [p];
            Back => [p];
            Coplanar => [p];
            Spanning => p.ClipToHalfSpace(pl).NonDegenerate
                .Concatenate(p.ClipToHalfSpace(pl.Flip).NonDegenerate);
        };
```
